summary: GRS-10H light bar continues to flash without active call
description: Multiple customers have reported light bars remaining illuminated/flashing after calls are canceled (expected behavior is to cease illuminating flashing). R&D has not been able to reproduce the error.

R&D developers suspect the cause is a multithreading bug in the modgrs10h handler which would update the lightbar state out of order. That theory would explain both (1) how the light bar becomes out-of-sync with the call status and (2) why rebooting the device resolves the issue in the field as explained in https://hill-rom.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1028. In layman’s terms, under certain conditions (which are difficult to replicate), programmed instructions that control lightbar illumination could execute out of the intended order.

The proposed fix in the Investigational Patch is twofold:

1. Change how the modgrs10h handler pushes lightbar actions to threads
2. ~~As a fallback, add a "LightbarEnabled" option in the /opt/local/hrapps/nnc/bin/env.json config file. This option turns the lightbar light off as long as the "LighbarEnabled" option is set to false.~~
comment_summary: The thread covers a field defect where the GRS-10H light bar continues to flash with no active call. Investigation identified an alert getting stuck on in the lightbar handler; the stuck alert does not preempt higher priority alerts, but once a higher priority alert clears the stale lower priority alert reappears. impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Before:  
The modgrs10h handler had a possible multithreading bug which would update the lightbar state out of order. If the last update of the alert is on, then the lightbar will remain on until the next nnc reboot.  
After:  
The modgrs10h handler now pushes all lightbar actions to the correct thread, and looks up the most recent data instead of relying on possibly stale alert data. This should resolve any issues with the lightbar using old or out of order alert data to decide its state.

Impact Assessment:  
NNC - Call Placement and Handling - Minor: functionality should not be impacted except for the extremely rare bug specific to the lightbar, which is attempted to be fixed in this IP

Platform Impact:  
GRS10h

Regression Meeting:  
Date:  17/DEC/2024  
Attendees - Stephen Moore (Development Engineering), Bhargav Bhalodia (Quality Engineering), Kyle Willey (Quality Engineering)  
Minutes - Group discussed test coverage and strategy to try to surface a possible reproduction strategy for the direct test being created. Regressions are largely identified out of filter though the identified Impact area is considered the most appropriate for the Defect. Most of the testing in filter covers call placement and handling functionality unrelated to the GRS10h Lightbar. Supplemental tests specific to GRS10h Lightbar were added for suitable regression coverage. See CWS-FLD-4365 GRS10H Lightbar in Jama.

comment_summary: A CCD GRS10 console was spiking in CPU and generating Lost Primary Console alerts. Syslogs and advanced service logs were collected and the console stabilised after the plugins enabled on it and the secondary monitored locations were temporarily removed; the combination of enabled plugins and the number of monitored units was identified as the cause of the spiking. The recommendation given was to add a second GRS10 CCD to split the workload if the site adds more rooms or units, though the thread notes there is no published specification for how many devices a CCD can monitor. A later comment links this behaviour to another RCA, suggesting removing monitored units helps because it removes the ability for the message to bounce around in the system.

summary: GRS-10H light bar continues to flash without active call
description: Multiple customers have reported light bars remaining illuminated/flashing after calls are canceled (expected behavior is to cease illuminating flashing). R&D has not been able to reproduce the error.

R&D developers suspect the cause is a multithreading bug in the modgrs10h handler which would update the lightbar state out of order. In layman’s terms, under certain conditions (which are difficult to replicate), programmed instructions that control lightbar illumination could execute out of the intended order.

The proposed fix in the Investigational Patch is twofold:

1. Change how the modgrs10h handler pushes lightbar actions to threads
2. ~~As a fallback, add a "LightbarEnabled" option in the /opt/local/hrapps/nnc/bin/env.json config file. This option turns the lightbar light off as long as the "LighbarEnabled" option is set to false.~~

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Before:  
The modgrs10h handler had a possible multithreading bug which would update the lightbar state out of order. If the last update of the alert is on, then the lightbar will remain on until the next nnc reboot.  
After:  
The modgrs10h handler now pushes all lightbar actions to the correct thread, and looks up the most recent data instead of relying on possibly stale alert data. This should resolve any issues with the lightbar using old or out of order alert data to decide its state.

Impact Assessment:  
NNC - Call Placement and Handling - Minor: functionality should not be impacted except for the extremely rare bug specific to the lightbar, which is attempted to be fixed in this IP

Platform Impact:  
GRS10h

Regression Meeting:  
Date:  17/DEC/2024  
Attendees - Stephen Moore (Development Engineering), Bhargav Bhalodia (Quality Engineering), Kyle Willey (Quality Engineering)  
Minutes - Group discussed test coverage and strategy to try to surface a possible reproduction strategy for the direct test being created. Regressions are largely identified out of filter though the identified Impact area is considered the most appropriate for the Defect. Most of the testing in filter covers call placement and handling functionality unrelated to the GRS10h Lightbar. Supplemental tests specific to GRS10h Lightbar were added for suitable regression coverage. See CWS-FLD-4365 GRS10H Lightbar in Jama.

summary: GRS-10H light bar continues to flash without active call
description: Multiple customers have reported light bars remaining illuminated/flashing after calls are canceled (expected behavior is to cease illuminating flashing). R&D has not been able to reproduce the error.

R&D developers suspect the cause is a multithreading bug in the modgrs10h handler which would update the lightbar state out of order. That theory would explain both (1) how the light bar becomes out-of-sync with the call status and (2) why rebooting the device resolves the issue in the field as explained in https://hill-rom.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1028. In layman’s terms, under certain conditions (which are difficult to replicate), programmed instructions that control lightbar illumination could execute out of the intended order.

The proposed fix in the Investigational Patch is twofold:

1. Change how the modgrs10h handler pushes lightbar actions to threads
2. ~~As a fallback, add a "LightbarEnabled" option in the /opt/local/hrapps/nnc/bin/env.json config file. This option turns the lightbar light off as long as the "LighbarEnabled" option is set to false.~~
comment_summary: The thread covers a field defect where the GRS-10H light bar continues to flash with no active call. Investigation identified an alert getting stuck on in the lightbar handler; the stuck alert does not preempt higher priority alerts, but once a higher priority alert clears the stale lower priority alert reappears. An investigational patch built as an emb-base-package GRS10H-only build was deployed to a customer site and appeared to resolve the problem, and a later bugfix build was produced for dry run. The team decided not to commercialize the contingency LightbarEnabled configuration option, added call placement and handling tests to regression, and closed the defect after all tests passed and the fix was verified.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Before:  
The modgrs10h handler had a possible multithreading bug which would update the lightbar state out of order. If the last update of the alert is on, then the lightbar will remain on until the next nnc reboot.  
After:  
The modgrs10h handler now pushes all lightbar actions to the correct thread, and looks up the most recent data instead of relying on possibly stale alert data. This should resolve any issues with the lightbar using old or out of order alert data to decide its state.

summary: GRS-10H light bar continues to flash without active call
description: Multiple customers have reported light bars remaining illuminated/flashing after calls are canceled (expected behavior is to cease illuminating flashing). R&D has not been able to reproduce the error.

R&D developers suspect the cause is a multithreading bug in the modgrs10h handler which would update the lightbar state out of order. That theory would explain both (1) how the light bar becomes out-of-sync with the call status and (2) why rebooting the device resolves the issue in the field as explained in https://hill-rom.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1028. In layman’s terms, under certain conditions (which are difficult to replicate), programmed instructions that control lightbar illumination could execute out of the intended order.

The proposed fix in the Investigational Patch is twofold:

1. Change how the modgrs10h handler pushes lightbar actions to threads
2. ~~As a fallback, add a "LightbarEnabled" option in the /opt/local/hrapps/nnc/bin/env.json config file. This option turns the lightbar light off as long as the "LighbarEnabled" option is set to false.~~
comment_summary: The thread covers a field defect where the GRS-10H light bar continues to flash with no active call. Investigation identified an alert getting stuck on in the lightbar handler; the stuck alert does not preempt higher priority alerts, but once a higher priority alert clears the stale lower priority alert reappears. An investigational patch built as an emb-base-package GRS10H-only build was deployed to a customer site and appeared to resolve the problem, and a later bugfix build was produced for dry run. The team decided not to commercialize the contingency LightbarEnabled configuration option, added call placement and handling tests to regression, and closed the defect after all tests passed and the fix was verified.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Before:  
The modgrs10h handler had a possible multithreading bug which would update the lightbar state out of order. If the last update of the alert is on, then the lightbar will remain on until the next nnc reboot.  
After:  
The modgrs10h handler now pushes all lightbar actions to the correct thread, and looks up the most recent data instead of relying on possibly stale alert data. This should resolve any issues with the lightbar using old or out of order alert data to decide its state.

Impact Assessment:  
NNC - Call Placement and Handling - Minor: functionality should not be impacted except for the extremely rare bug specific to the lightbar, which is attempted to be fixed in this IP

Platform Impact:

Regressions are largely identified out of filter though the identified Impact area is considered the most appropriate for the Defect. Most of the testing in filter covers call placement and handling functionality unrelated to the GRS10h Lightbar. Supplemental tests specific to GRS10h Lightbar were added for suitable regression coverage. See CWS-FLD-4365 GRS10H Lightbar in Jama.

root_cause_summary: The connector should be modified to only raise button press events if there is one in the ModelUpdate.Events collection.
investigation_details: When the connector starts (or even when a tag is discovered and the connector is already running or when the connector re-connects), the HPL system will send an initial state of the tag to the rtls connector.  The RTLS connector will receive that message and, because it has a “buttonPress”, it’ll interpret it as a click even though the message also indicates the button press occurred at the beginning of time. So, every time the RTLS Connector disconnects and re-connects to HPL, we’d get one of these mass reporting events; with every single tag that’s assigned at that moment generating a duress call.

HPL does not re-set the timestamp back to `DateTime.MinValue` (ever). So it’ll only be that value if the button has never been clicked. So this fix could get tricky as you’d need to make a decision based on the last time the tag reported. Or something. I’d be happy to rubber duck solution options.

Investigation of the RTLS connector logs found Centrak sending duplicate button events in the same data packet (entries ending 'button2, button2'), and the IntegrationService log showed the IHEAdapter repeatedly failing to reach a development host with "The remote name could not be resolved: 'hi-dev-nnc1.hrdev.io'", a value hard-coded in the app config that applies to all sites without a PCD-05 integration.
